subject: math
intro: Formal constructions use only a compass and an unmarked straightedge, no measuring. Standard constructions include: copying a segment, copying an angle, bisecting a segment (which also builds its perpendicular bisector), bisecting an angle, constructing a line perpendicular to a given line through a point, and constructing a line parallel to a given line through a point. These rely on the properties of circles (all radii equal) and the fact that intersecting arcs create equidistant points.

items.prompt: Which two tools are allowed in a formal geometric construction?

steps: Only a compass and an unmarked straightedge are used.
So the tools are a compass and a straightedge.

items.prompt: When you bisect a segment with compass and straightedge, what line do you also create?

steps: Bisecting finds the midpoint using equal arcs from both endpoints.
The crossing arcs lie on the line perpendicular to the segment at its midpoint.
So you also construct the perpendicular bisector.
solution.answer: The perpendicular bisector of the segment.

items.prompt: Why does a compass help construct equal lengths?

steps: A compass keeps a fixed opening (radius).
All points drawn at that opening are the same distance from the center.
So the compass reproduces equal lengths exactly.
solution.answer: Because all radii of a compass circle are equal, it reproduces equal lengths.

items.prompt: What tools are used in formal constructions?

steps: Only a compass and an unmarked straightedge.
Common constructions include copying and bisecting.
For example, copying a segment and bisecting an angle.
solution.answer: Copying a segment and bisecting an angle (others vary).

items.prompt: Bisecting a segment also produces what special line?

steps: The bisection uses equal arcs from both ends.
